description.narrative:
Mahidol University (Nakhon Pathom, Thailand) in collaboration with ASEAN University Network - Human Rights and Education (AUN-HRE, Nakhon Pathom, Thailand) and Southeast Asian Human Rights Studies Network (SEAHRN, Depok, Indonesia), has applied to Sida for support for a regional research network in the field of human rights and peace studies. The project proposal is entitled: Strengthening human rights and peace research and education in ASEAN / Southeast Asia (SHAPE-SEA): Funding proposal for program phase 2 (July 2021-December 2024). The SHAPE-SEA research network and its activities will be implemented regionally in Southeast Asia, with a special focus on Cambodia, Laos, Vietnam and East Timor, where the research capacity for peace and human rights studies is assessed to require further support.
The SHAPE-SEA Phase 2 contribution will build upon the results achieved during SHAPE-SEA phase 1 (2015 - 2021). The Sida grant will enable the SHAPE-SEA Secretariat at Mahidol University to strengthen research capacity amongst Southeast Asian peace and human rights researchers, and to strengthen respect for academic freedom in Southeast Asia. The grant will also support Southeast Asian peace and human rights researchers to 1) produce new knowledge, 2) engage with regional and national stakeholders to implement research results, and 3) contribute to public human rights discourses. and peace in Southeast Asia.
Research scholarships will be awarded to researchers in the region to carry out research projects that study local, national and cross-border research issues related to peace and human rights. The research results and research capacity generated by the initiative will contribute to improved conditions for fair and sustainable development that is inclusive of vulnerable and marginalized groups in Southeast Asia.
The total budget of the contribution during July 2021 - December 2024 is 16,6 million SEK. Approximately 2,7 million SEK of the funding will be forwarded from Mahidol University to researchers at Southeast Asian universities and research organizations in the form of small scholarships to support research activities.

Mahidol universitet (Nakhon Pathom, Thailand) i samarbete med ASEAN University Network - Human Rights and Education (AUN-HRE, Nakhon Pathom, Thailand) och Southeast Asian Human Rights Studies Network (SEAHRN, Depok, Indonesien), har ansökt om stöd för ett regionalt forskningsnätverk inom teman mänskliga rättigheter och fred. Projektförslaget är Strengthening human rights and peace research and education in ASEAN/Southeast Asia (SHAPE-SEA) Phase 2 (July 2021-December 2024). SHAPE-SEA forskningsnätverket och dess verksamhet kommer att arbeta regionalt i Sydostasien, med särskilt fokus på Kambodja, Laos, Vietnam och Öst Timor där forskningskapacitet inom fred och mänskliga rättigheter bedöms som i behov av ytterligare stöd.
SHAPE-SEA Phase 2 kommer att bygga vidare på resultaten som uppnåddes under SHAPE-SEA Phase 1 (2015-2021). Sida-bidraget gör det möjligt för SHAPE-SEA sekretariatet vid Mahidol University att stärka forskningskapaciteten bland sydostasiatiska forskare inom freds- och mänskliga rättighetsstudier. Projektet kommer också att stödja sydostasiatiska forskare att ta fram ny kunskap, samarbeta med regionala och nationella aktörer för att genomföra forskningsresultat och bidra till offentliga diskurser om mänskliga rättigheter och fred i Sydostasien.
Forskningsstipendier kommer att delas ut till forskare i regionen för att genomföra forskningsprojekt som studerar lokala, nationella och gränsöverskridande forskningsfrågor relaterade till fred och mänskliga rättigheter. De forskningsresultat och forskningskapacitet som initiativet genererar kommer att bidra till förbättrade förutsättningar för en rättvis och hållbar utveckling som inkluderar sårbara och marginaliserade grupper i Sydostasien.
Insatsens totala budget under juli 2021 - december 2024 är 16,6 miljoner SEK. Cirka 2,7 miljoner SEK kommer at vidareförmedlas från Mahidol universitet i form av mindre forskningsstipendier till forskare vid sydostasiatiska universitet och forskningsorganisationer för forskningsverksamhet.

The overall objectives of SHAPE-SEA Phase 2 are:
- to support and strengthen homegrown academic interest, skills and knowledge on researching human rights and peace in ASEAN/Southeast Asia.
- to create change by enhancing, influencing and translating policies, processes and practices of human rights and peace into action in ASEAN/Southeast Asia
- to ensure excellence in producing, disseminating, and analyzing knowledge on human rights and peace in ASEAN/Southeast Asia
- to further developing ways and means to internalizing human rights and peace knowledge amongst teaching staff, academic leaders and students in Higher Education Institutions in ASEAN/Southeast Asia

Key results achieved by SHAPESEA across four main outcomes in 2024 were:
i) Increasing Research Capacity
This program component aims at training and preparing potential researchers in the region for research grant opportunities organizing research skill training & workshops and ensuring quality mentorship to guide researchers through a resource pool of mentors. Under 2024, two research capacity training seminars for emerging scholars in Southeast Asia were organized on the themes Internalizing Human Rights, Democracy and Peace in Southeast Asia with 52 attendants and Introduction to Basic Concepts in Peace and Conflict in Advancing Research Capacity among Mekong Regions Emerging Scholars with 26 participants. Scholarship grantees were equipped with research skills and enhanced knowledge to address human rights and peace/conflict issues of relevance to their local, national and regional concerns. Participants were from Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand and Vietnam, of which 57.7% were women. The participant composition based on degree was 19.2% with PhD, 69.2% with masters degree and 11.5% bachelors degree. Many of the participants came from underrepresented universities and remote areas of Southeast Asia and the Mekong subregion.
A Research Grant Programme (RGP) capacity training to the 15 new scholarship grantees enrolled in 2024 were organized in August 2024 to equip their research skills and enhance knowledge to address human rights and peace/conflict issues of relevance to their local, national and regional context. The scholarship grantees were selected from an application review process of 120 applicants. The 15 research grantees were selected across multiple disciplines and 8 Southeast Asian countries (Philippines, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam).
ii) Knowledge Production This program component aims at developing collaborative projects across Southeast Asia academic institutions and disciplines grants scheme support context specific and transformative research on human rights and peace and incorporating innovative, intersectional approaches to research themes. The 2024 Research Grant Program (RGP) was launched with 15 new scholarship grantees. The themes most covered by their research projects are related to gender & sexuality, peace & conflict, cultures, values and identities, environment justice & conflicts, food security and land ownership, indigenous livelihoods, labour rights.
SHAPE-SEA also conducted research visits during 2024 to provide technical and substantive support to its researchers. These visits took place in Mindanao in the Philippines (January), Yogyakarta in Indonesia (February), and Hanoi in Vietnam (June). These face to face engagements helped foster direct interactions with Grantees, enabling real-time feedback and tailored support for each research projects, and collaboration with local institutions and university students with seminars to promote the RGP opportunities to them.
iii) Knowledge Dissemination The 6th Southeast Asian Human Rights Network (SEAHRN) International Conference organized by SHAPE-SEA during 13-14 August 2024 was the most prominent activity in knowledge dissemination of the year. The main theme of the conference was on Peace and Human Rights in Southeast Asia in the Context of Contemporary Global Crises, which brought together 193 participants (152 onsite) including academics, researchers, graduate and postgraduate students, CSOs, and government representatives from Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam, and India, Japan, Taiwan and others. Intersecting topics discussed and presented at the conference were related to Global governance & democracy, human rights and rule of law, global health and human rights, women, peace and security, climate& business and human rights gender and sexuality, marginalized groups, environmental conflict and rights. Other parallel panels were dealt with such as China Investment on Nickel Mining Industries in Indonesia (DRC compared), Peace & Conflict in Southern Thailand, and Peace Promotion in Myanmar.
SHAPE-SEA's flagship Human Rights Outlook in Southeast Asia 2023 was launched on 11 December 2024 at Mahidol University. The publication was unveiled during a public panel discussing the regions progress and challenges in upholding the Universal Declaration of Human Rights. This launch served as a key highlight in commemorating International Human Rights Day. The topics highlighted in this Southeast Asia Human Rights Outlook cover: Civil and Political Rights, Economic, Social and Cultural rights Academic freedom Vulnerable and Marginalized Groups Migration and Refugee Rights, Human Rights Violation, Gender, Environmental and Climate Rights. The outlook is assessed by its stakeholders and researchers to have of impact and usefulness for academic research, policy development, advocacy and teaching materials relevant to Southeast Asian region.
